title: Class 6 Science · Ch 2 Worksheet A · Plant Classification
instructions: Practise identifying types of plants by stem, leaf, and root.

questions.question: A short plant with a soft, green stem is called
questions.explanation: Herbs are short plants with soft stems (e.g., tulsi).

questions.question: Plants with a single main thick root and side branches have a
questions.explanation: Taproots have one main root with smaller side roots.

questions.question: Leaves with veins running side by side are said to have
questions.explanation: Parallel venation is seen in grass, maize, etc.

questions.question: A medium-sized plant with a hard, branching stem near the base is called a _____.
questions.explanation: Rose and lemon are common shrubs.

questions.question: A seed that splits into two halves is called a _____.
questions.explanation: Dicots have two cotyledons (e.g., gram, mango).

questions.question: Plants with reticulate venation usually have a fibrous root system.
questions.explanation: Reticulate venation is paired with taproots; parallel venation goes with fibrous roots.

questions.question: How would you tell a herb from a tree by looking at it?
questions.answer: A herb is short with a soft, green stem. A tree is tall with a thick, hard, woody stem.

questions.question: You find a plant with reticulate-veined leaves. Predict what type of root system and seed structure it likely has, with reasons.
questions.answer: It likely has a taproot and dicot seeds. Reticulate venation (net-like veins) is typically paired with taproots and dicots in plant classification.
questions.explanation: Tests applying the link between visual features and underlying classification.

questions.question: Make a chart of 6 common plants in your area. For each, note: name, herb/shrub/tree, leaf venation, and dicot/monocot.
questions.answer: Sample chart: Tulsi — herb — reticulate — dicot. Rose — shrub — reticulate — dicot. Mango — tree — reticulate — dicot. Grass — herb — parallel — monocot. Maize — herb — parallel — monocot. Hibiscus — shrub — reticulate — dicot. Any 6 plants with consistent classifications accepted.
questions.explanation: Tests creating a classification chart from observations.
